author: DTrim99
body:
Same root cause as #1110 — PolicyEngine applies the $12,000 married pension-exclusion cap per spouse instead of as the combined limit ("a married couple is allowed a combined exclusion of up to $12,000," 2021 Expanded Instructions p. 27). Your read is exactly right. Tracked in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9155 with the fix in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9156, which prorates the single $12,000 across eligible spouses by pension share, as TaxAct does here.

Re-running this record with that fix applied, everything reconciles with the TaxAct return: net income 138,890 vs 69,445 + 69,444 = 138,889; taxable income 108,739 on both sides; tax before credits 5,712.90 vs 2,857 + 2,857 = 5,714; and after the $160 of exemption credits, 5,552.90 vs 5,554 — differences are whole-dollar rounding. We'll flag here once the fix is in a released policyengine-us version.
